questions.q: What does traditional signature-based antivirus compare a file against to decide it's malicious?
options: A database of known malware hashes or byte patterns collected from previously-seen malware
A list of every process currently running on the endpoint
A live behavioral analysis of what the file does once it runs
A record of which user account owns the file
questions.explain: Signature-based antivirus scans a file and checks it against a database of hashes/patterns from malware that's already been catalogued.

questions.q: What is the main blind spot of signature-based detection?
options: It can only scan files smaller than a certain size
Zero-day, polymorphic, and fileless malware that have no matching signature to compare against
It cannot quarantine or delete any file it finds
It only works on Windows and never on any other operating system
questions.explain: Anything that hasn't been catalogued yet — zero-day malware, self-rewriting polymorphic malware, or fileless attacks with no file to scan — slips past signature matching entirely.

questions.q: What does an EDR agent primarily monitor on an endpoint?
options: Only the hashes of files saved to the desktop
Continuous behavioral telemetry: process creation, process trees, network connections, and file/registry changes
The physical temperature and hardware health of the device
Only traffic that passes through a network firewall
questions.explain: EDR streams behavioral telemetry off the endpoint and builds a process tree, instead of inspecting static files for a known hash.

questions.q: What does the "response" half of EDR add beyond what traditional antivirus does?
options: The ability to isolate a live host from the network, kill a running process remotely, and pull a forensic timeline
The ability to block a user's login for 24 hours
Nothing — EDR and antivirus respond to threats in exactly the same way
The ability to automatically reinstall the operating system
questions.explain: Traditional antivirus response is limited to quarantine/delete. EDR gives analysts real actions on a running endpoint: isolation, remote process termination, and forensic investigation.

questions.q: In the fileless phishing example, why does signature-based antivirus miss the attack while EDR catches it?
options: No file is ever written to disk for antivirus to scan, but the process tree of Word spawning PowerShell with an outbound connection is visible to EDR
EDR scans faster than antivirus, so it just gets there first
The attack only happens on Linux, where antivirus doesn't run
Antivirus was simply turned off on the affected machine
questions.explain: The payload runs entirely in memory, leaving nothing for a file scanner to examine — but the sequence of process behavior it creates is exactly what EDR's telemetry is built to flag.
